title: Admin compliance toggles: IP allowlist, disable public sharing, and export controls
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and regulated orgs need fine-grained admin controls that can be toggled at the org level to enforce compliance policies. Current console lacks a single place for enabling IP allowlisting, disabling public sharing (links and public model endpoints), and preventing bulk data exports. These controls must integrate with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML enforcement, and produce immutable audit logs.

Proposed work: Add an "Org Compliance" section in the Redwood Console and corresponding admin APIs. Expose three toggles: (1) IP Allowlisting (CIDR list) with enforcement at the API gateway and ingress load balancer, (2) Disable Public Sharing which turns off creation of public share links and public model endpoints, and (3) Data Export Controls which disables bulk export APIs and UI exports and marks export attempts in the audit log with reason codes. Tie each toggle to RBAC v2 permission checks so only org admins can change them and so service roles can be exempted where needed. Ensure SSO/SAML enforced sessions cannot circumvent toggles (session refreshes validate org flags). All changes must be recorded in audit logs with actor, IP, old_value, new_value, timestamp, and justification when provided.

Scope: console UI, admin API endpoints, API gateway enforcement rules, auth middleware changes (RBAC v2 integration), audit log schema updates, e2e tests, migration for existing orgs where default is "off". Excluded: per-project toggles (this is org-level only) and automated remediation workflows (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Console: Org Compliance page available under Organization Settings with three toggles and inline help text
API: Admin endpoints exist to read/update the three toggles and return effective settings including exemptions
Enforcement: API gateway rejects requests that violate IP allowlist with 403 and audit log entry
Public sharing: Attempts to create public links/endpoints return 403 when disabled and are logged
Data export: Bulk/export endpoints and UI export buttons are disabled or hidden and any attempted export is recorded in audit logs with a reason code
RBAC: Only users with org_admin role per RBAC v2 can update toggles; changes are validated against policy engine
SSO/SAML: Session validation re-checks org compliance flags and prevents token use to bypass controls
Audit logs: All toggle changes and enforcement events are write-once, include actor, IP, old/new values, justification, and are queryable via audit API
Tests: Unit, integration, and e2e test coverage included and green on CI
Docs: Console help doc and API docs updated with examples and migration notes
comments: 2026-02-13 - Anya Patel: Initial ticket created after a customer audit flagged lack of org-level export controls. Added proposed scope and acceptance criteria.

2026-02-18 - Marcus Lee: Implementation plan draft - will add a feature flag for gradual rollout and a migration job to tag existing orgs. Gateway enforcement requires ACL rules change; coordinating with infra team.
2026-02-22 - Priya Shah (Product): Reviewed UX copy and asked for inline justification field when toggles are changed. Suggested we add 'grace period' opt-out for orgs migrating to stricter policies.

2026-03-01 - Security review (notes): Must ensure audit logs are tamper-evident and retention align with customer retention settings. Recommend HMAC signing for records and KMS key usage. Also require a short diagram for threat model.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Lee: PR opened - github.com/redwood-inference/rw-console/pull/1427 implementing UI and API. Backend enforcement branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-gateway/tree/feature/compliance-toggles. E2E tests added in rw-e2e tests.

2026-03-08 - QA: Found a race where a token cached in edge layer bypasses newest allowlist for ~30s. Mitigation: invalidate edge token cache on policy change and add a short TTL; infra to provide mechanism.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Lee: Addressed QA race by adding policy-change webhook to invalidate caches. Updated acceptance criteria to include cache invalidation verification. Marking ticket ready for security re-review.
notes: Trade-offs considered: Centralized enforcement at the gateway simplifies policy surface but increases gateway complexity and risk during rollout. Alternative was enforcement at the service layer per-route; rejected because it leaves gaps for non-standard endpoints. Rollout strategy: dark-launch enforcement rules first, then enable blocking for a small set of pilot orgs, then org-by-org ramp with migrations docs.
test_plan: Unit tests for API, integration tests for gateway rejection and audit record creation, e2e test simulating SSO session and toggle change, manual validation steps for pilot orgs
risks: Potential latency bump at API gateway for IP checks; token cache invalidation window causing short bypass; incorrect RBAC mapping could allow unauthorized changes. Mitigations include caching TTL, telemetry to track blocked calls, and a canary rollout.
